reuse.why: Builds on the existing getWeekendAdjustedDay, getNextDate, recurConfigToRSchedule and month utils, and adds shared helpers (isWeekendOrHoliday, getDailyLookahead, getMaxShiftDays) that the consumers import rather than recomputing.

duplication.why: The daily-skip decision (frequency === 'daily' && skipWeekend) and the filter of weekend/holiday occurrences, plus the 'skipWeekend && !skipsDailyWeekend' argument to getWeekendAdjustedDay, are repeated in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange instead of living in one helper.

placement.why: Holiday and adjustment rules sit in shared/schedules.ts and the new handler in server/schedules/app.ts, matching the tree, but the skip-vs-move policy for daily schedules is decided by each caller.

scope.why: Changes are confined to the schedule date rules, the new handler, the template loop that consumes them, and tests.

maintainability.why: Shared adjustment and bound helpers are clean, but a maintainer changing which frequencies skip, or how skipped days are filtered, must update three call sites plus the schedule-template flag in step.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange (server/schedules/app.ts) and getNextDate (shared/schedules.ts) each decide the daily skip and filter occurrences themselves around getWeekendAdjustedDay; schedule-template.ts toggles getNextDate's noSkipWeekend flag by its own isDaily check.

disguised_duplication.where: The occurrence filter is written as dates.filter in getNextDate, as .filter(...).slice in getUpcomingDates and as a for/continue loop in getDatesInRange; the skipsDailyWeekend predicate is repeated in each.

abstraction_drift.where: getWeekendAdjustedDay gains a holidays option (no special cases inside it); the daily-skip rule is applied outside it at getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and the schedule-template loop (isDaily → noSkipWeekend).
